newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta suppressed by strong mark in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Peseta suppressed by strong mark in late trade.

text.p: The peseta softened against the mark in late Tuesday trade as the German currency was buoyed by a German government official's remarks about EMU.
By 1650 GMT, the peseta was at 84.40/41 per mark, compared with levels seen late on Monday of 84.16/18.

The mark jumped, especially against the lira, after comments by German state secretary to the finance ministry Juergen Stark that some qualifiers would be well advised to delay EMU entry and that there are "no forgone conclusions."
While Stark did not name names, analysts said his comments appeared directed at countries like Italy and Spain.
One trader warned that if the peseta slipped much further, the central bank may be tempted to intervene.
"The central bank may wish to hold the currency steady and could soon decide to buy pesetas," he said.
Against the dollar, the peseta also softened to 139.10/15 compared with 138.08/13 late on Monday.
